articles.title: Hackers Used Meta’s AI Support Bot to Seize Instagram Accounts
articles.summary: Microsoft drops a record-breaking 200 patches this Patch Tuesday, with three dozen rated critical — because apparently Redmond was saving up all year for one spectacular vulnerability Christmas morning.

articles.title: Victory! 702 has Expired!
articles.summary: CISA contractor casually dumps AWS GovCloud keys on public GitHub like it's their personal blog, prompting Congress to ask the obvious question: what the actual hell, guys?

articles.title: Yes to California's Bill to Ban Surveillance Pricing
articles.summary: Section 702's warrantless surveillance authority finally expires, meaning the government will have to find new creative ways to violate the Fourth Amendment.

articles.title: Claude Fable 5 Doesn't Change the Mythos Security Story
articles.summary: ShinyHunters exploits Oracle ERP zero-day to ransack university networks nationwide. Higher education meets higher exploitation — tuition money well spent, clearly.

articles.title: U.S. Orders Anthropic to Suspend Fable 5 and Mythos 5 Access for Foreign Nationals
articles.summary: Critical Splunk Enterprise flaw (CVE-2026-20253) allows unauthenticated remote code execution with a perfect 9.8 CVSS score. Even your logs aren't safe anymore.

articles.title: Google Sues Chinese Smishing Network Accused of Using Gemini AI in Phishing
articles.summary: Attackers hijack 400+ Arch Linux AUR packages to deploy credential stealers and eBPF rootkits. Linux elitists discover their package repository isn't as secure as their smugness suggested.

articles.title: Twenty One Zero-Days in FFmpeg
articles.summary: Chinese Velvet Ant group backdoors Linux PAM and OpenSSH for nearly a decade, proving that sometimes the best place to hide is right in the front door.

articles.title: The new BitLocker exploit everyone's freaking out about probably won't affect you
articles.summary: Autonomous security agent discovers 21 zero-days in FFmpeg after Google and Anthropic's analysis missed them. AI vs AI — may the best bot win.

articles.title: Oracle Addresses PeopleSoft Vulnerability Amid Reports of Zero-Day Attacks
articles.summary: Oracle warns of security bug exploited in mass-hacking campaign targeting 100+ companies. When Oracle issues security warnings, you know it's either very serious or very embarrassing.

articles.title: The Hidden Security Risks of Poor Software Testing
articles.summary: Oracle scrambles to address CVE-2026-35273 PeopleSoft vulnerability amid ShinyHunters zero-day attacks. PeopleSoft living up to its reputation as enterprise software that makes people soft targets.
